common_name: Spice Girl Viburnum (Full-Size Proven Winners Koreanspice Viburnum)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in late winter or early spring in moist, well-drained soil in part to full sun; old-wood flower buds should be left undisturbed until right after bloom if any shaping is needed.

directions: Spice Girl is a full-size Proven Winners selection of Korean spice viburnum, reaching 6 to 7 feet tall and wide at maturity and carrying the same intensely fragrant, pink-tinged white flower clusters that make the species a dooryard favorite each spring. Plant where its old-wood flower buds are sheltered from late hard freezes, since pruning right after bloom preserves next year's display. Green summer foliage shifts to red and burgundy tones in fall, adding a second season of interest beyond the fragrant bloom.

common_name: Spice Cowboy Viburnum (Large-Flowered Proven Winners Koreanspice Viburnum)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in late winter or early spring in moist, well-drained soil in part to full sun; allow its upright habit room to reach full height without crowding.

directions: Spice Cowboy carries unusually large, snowball-like flower clusters for a Korean spice viburnum, packing an intense spicy-sweet fragrance onto an upright plant that can reach 10 feet given time. Its narrower spread compared to height suits it to tight side-yard plantings or as a tall hedge component where width is limited. Summer's clean green foliage turns a vivid orange-red in autumn, and like other Korean spice selections it flowers on old wood, so prune only right after the spring bloom fades.

common_name: Asian Beauty Linden Viburnum (Heavy Red-Fruited Linden Viburnum)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained, average soil in full sun; a genetically distinct cultivar or seedling nearby improves fruit set.

directions: Asian Beauty is prized among linden viburnum selections for the sheer profusion and winter persistence of its cherry-red fruit, which forms dense clusters after the creamy white, flat-topped flower clusters fade in late spring. Like most Viburnum dilatatum, it sets the heaviest fruit crop when a genetically distinct seedling or cultivar is planted nearby for cross-pollination. Its upright, rounded habit and clean summer foliage make it a strong multi-season anchor for a mixed shrub border or naturalized planting.

common_name: Anne Russell Viburnum (Compact Fragrant Burkwood Hybrid)

planting.note: Plant container or balled-and-burlapped shrubs in early spring in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; blooms on old wood, so prune only right after flowering finishes.

directions: Anne Russell is a backcross of Viburnum x burkwoodii with Viburnum carlesii, bred in England to combine Korean spice viburnum's fragrance with burkwood viburnum's vigor on a more compact, rounded frame. Pink buds open in mid-spring to clusters of white flowers carrying a spicy-sweet perfume that rivals its Korean spice parent. Glossy dark green summer leaves turn crimson-purple in autumn, giving the shrub a strong finish after the fragrant spring display fades.

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained soil in full sun; deadheading is not needed to keep the rebloom cycle going.

directions: Crimson Kisses produces lipstick-red, trumpet-shaped flowers with a contrasting white eye against dark green foliage from late spring into fall. Its mounded, well-contained habit tops out around 3 to 4 feet, making it a better fit for small gardens and foundation plantings than older full-size weigela cultivars. The nectar-rich flowers draw hummingbirds throughout the growing season, and light shearing after the first flush encourages further rebloom.

common_name: Maroon Swoon Weigela (Deep Red Weigela, Slingco 2)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained soil in full sun; light shearing after the main spring flush encourages the next wave of flowers.

directions: Maroon Swoon is a compact weigela selection valued for deep red, trumpet-shaped flowers set off by a small white eye, carried against foliage with a dark maroon cast through the growing season. Its compact, rounded form fits well in mixed shrub borders and foundation plantings where full-size weigela would crowd the space. Rebloom continues sporadically from late spring into fall, keeping color in the garden well past the main spring flush.

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained soil in full sun; full sun brings out the richest foliage color and heaviest bloom.

directions: Stunner pairs vivid pink, trumpet-shaped flowers with deep burgundy-purple foliage that holds its color from spring through frost, giving the plant strong ornamental value even between bloom cycles. It keeps a compact, rounded habit well under the size of older weigela cultivars, suiting small gardens and mixed borders. Light pruning right after the heaviest spring flush maintains a tidy shape without sacrificing later bud set.
